title: Mandibular Osteonecrosis: Imaging and Biomarkers
summary: In diseases such as osteoradionecrosis, medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw, and chronic jaw inflammation, bone in the lower jaw dies off. Before surgery, these conditions are usually examined using imaging techniques such as MRI and CT. This study aims to find out how well these images reflect the actual biological changes in the bone – such as blood supply and bone remodeling. To do this, bone samples are taken during surgery from patients who are undergoing an operation anyway, and these are compared with the imaging findings. The goal is to better understand the imaging and, in the future, enable more precise and tissue-sparing surgical planning.

interventions.name: Arm 1: Adult patients with osteoradionecrosis (ORN) of the mandible, in whom a routine preoperative MRI (T1W and T2WFS sequences) and CT are performed and an intraoperative bone sample is collected for histological/immunohistochemical examination.

Arm 2: Adult patients with medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) of the mandible, in whom a routine preoperative MRI (T1W and T2WFS sequences) and CT are performed and an intraoperative bone sample is collected for histological/immunohistochemical examination.

Arm 3: Adult patients with chronic mandibular osteomyelitis (CMO), in whom a routine preoperative MRI (T1W and T2WFS sequences) and CT are performed and an intraoperative bone sample is collected for histological/immunohistochemical examination.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years; confirmed diagnosis of ORN, MRONJ, or CMO; capacity to provide consent; willingness to participate in imaging, surgery, and sample collection.
Exclusion criteria:
No definitive diagnosis; insufficient tissue samples; contraindications to MRI.
